conviction_note: Two peers printed after Molina last spoke and both read positive on Molina's lines: Elevance's Medicaid beat on July 1 rate actions and its ACA ran ahead, and UNH's MCR improved. Against that, consensus ($0.72-0.81) already sits at or above the ~$0.70 Q3 the company's own guide implies, the stock is +13.6% in 20 days and above the $209 mean target, and 7 of the last 8 prints fell, including the Q2 beat-and-raise (-9.7%). The findings sum to about zero, p_up is 52 and abs_move is 12.5 (implied 11.3, median reaction 12.1, a 2027 framing likely), so the scaled number is +0.5. The fundamental read leans to a beat (+8% vs the EPS bar), but this name's reaction function does not pay for beats, so the move number stays near zero.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS. Company-implied: FY2026 adjusted EPS guide of at least $5.25 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001179929/000117992926000036/moh2q26_er.htm) less 1H actuals of $3.86 (Q1 $2.35, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001179929/000117992926000020/moh1q26_er.htm, plus Q2 $1.51) leaves at least $1.39 for 2H, which the CFO said would be 'fairly evenly split' (Q2 call, https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/MOH/Q22026), so about $0.70 for Q3. That figure carries ~$0.50 of Florida contract G&A before revenue starts. Street: Zacks $0.72 on ~$10.93B revenue with a 93% Medicaid MCR (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/analyst-projections-key-metrics-reveal-121506448.html); Investing.com $0.79 on $10.86B, estimates down 4.28% over 60 days (https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/molina-healthcare-earnings-in-focus-as-medicaid-pressures-mount-93CH-4894077, 2026-10-21); Benzinga $0.78-0.81. The estimate sources differ by about 10% but all sit at or above the company-implied ~$0.70. The stock trades on the guide and the 2027 framing more than on the quarter.
positioning_check: Short interest 2,887,217 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 5.5% of 52.2M shares outstanding, 4.76 days to cover (5.84 at 09-15, 4.92 at 08-31) per https://equibles.com/stocks/moh/short-interest. Moderate, not a crowded short, so the squeeze discount on negatives is small. Baseline 25-delta skew is +0.12 vol points (neutral, 'balanced'). Put/call OI ratio 0.33 (call-heavy). Event-implied move 11.28% (straddle 14.04% over 30 days). Run-up +13.6% over 20 days and +2.8% over 5, 11.4% below the 52-week high and 75% above the low. Spot is above the $209 mean target on a consensus Hold (19 analysts). Michael Burry is a publicly known long since late 2025.

findings.finding: Elevance, Molina's largest listed Medicaid peer, reported Q3 2026 this morning (2026-10-21). Its Medicaid results beat its own outlook 'mainly from recent rate actions'. The CFO said the July 1 updates 'did provide greater support to the second half margins', full-year Medicaid margin is now 'slightly ahead' of guidance, and cost trend is 'elevated but broadly stable and consistent with Q2'. Molina's 2H guide assumed a ~1.9% ex-Florida Medicaid pre-tax margin with no rate increases and 5% trend, and a full-year 4% rate vs 5% trend, so similar mid-year rate actions in Molina's states would land above its guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Medicaid MCR is the line Molina trades on (100 bp of Medicaid MCR is about $5/share per the Q2 call). Q1 2026's beat on cost control bought +14.2%. Q2 2026's beat with an unchanged 92.9% Medicaid MCR guide fell 9.7% because Marketplace was cut. Q3 2025 (-17.5%) and Q4 2025 (-25.5%) both fell on Medicaid and Marketplace cost resets.
findings.why_not_priced: Elevance printed about 9 hours before Molina, after every estimate in the bar was set. If the market had read it as a Medicaid read-through, MOH would be up today. Instead it slid from $219.72 (10:32 ET, Investing.com) to $215.1 at the 17:10 UTC seal, tracking ELV's ~2% drop on the quality of its non-operating beat. The read-through on the Medicaid line looks to have been sold with ELV's headline rather than priced into MOH. Molina is ~90% Medicaid by premium, so the line matters far more to it than to ELV.
findings.independence: Partly shares a document with the Elevance ACA finding (same call), but a different line. UNH Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000731766/000073176626000255/earningsrelease3q26unh.htm) shows the consolidated MCR improving but gives no Medicaid margin. Molina's own Q2 call said off-cycle rate increases so far were 'small and within expectations', which caps this finding.

findings.finding: Elevance's Individual ACA business is 'tracking ahead of full-year expectations with a modestly higher margin'. Claims are developing favorably, the seasonal bronze cost ramp is arriving more slowly than expected, and its risk adjustment was accrued on September Wakely data. In July Molina cut Marketplace by $1.50/share to a -$0.75 FY loss and said it took a 'conservative pick' on risk adjustment while its view was 'evolving'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Marketplace was the line behind the July 2026 -9.7% (a $1.50 cut that wiped out a $1.50 Medicare raise) and the 2025 resets (-16.8% in July 2025 and -17.5% in October 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: It came out this morning, and ELV's stock fell on the quality of its beat, so no positive ACA read-through shows in MOH today (down intraday). If the market had priced a better Marketplace risk-adjustment true-up at Molina, MOH would have outperformed ELV today; it did not. This is a proxy: Molina said its retained ~280K members are adversely selected and higher-acuity than the market, which is why it is sized below the Medicaid read.
findings.independence: Same Elevance call as the Medicaid finding, different line. Centene's Q2 10-Q booked a $481M benefit from the final 2025 risk-adjustment transfers (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001071739/000107173926000153/cnc-20260630.htm), but that is benefit year 2025 and already in Molina's Q2.

findings.finding: UnitedHealth's Q3 2026 (2026-10-13) showed a consolidated MCR of 88.4% vs 89.9% a year earlier and ~89.9% expected, with $610M of favorable prior-period reserve development, and it raised FY adjusted EPS to at least $20.50. Community & State Medicaid membership fell to 6.695M (-10% YoY, -85K in the quarter).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sector read-through. UNH rose ~4.5% on its print, and MOH is up 6.3% over the month against a flat provider group (Yahoo preview).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: MOH has run +13.6% over 20 days, including a +3.8% day on 2026-10-12 attributed to managed-care sentiment (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Molina+Healthcare+Gains+as+Investors+Weigh+Sector+Tailwinds+and+Near-Term+Catalysts). What is left is the reserve-development signal that cost trend in 2026 dates of service is coming in benign, which would also show in Molina's prior-period development. Sized small because it is priced.
findings.independence: Separate document from the Elevance findings. https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/expect-molina-healthcare-moh-q3-063750358.html confirms the UNH reaction and MOH's run.

findings.finding: Consensus Q3 EPS of $0.72-0.81 (Zacks $0.72; Investing.com $0.79; Benzinga $0.78-0.81) sits at or up to ~15% above the ~$0.70 the company's own guide implies. That is FY at least $5.25, less 1H $3.86, giving at least $1.39 for 2H, 'fairly evenly split' per the CFO. The quarter also carries ~$0.50 of Florida CMS contract G&A before revenue starts on 10/1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Molina beat both 2026 quarters against consensus (Q1 $2.35; Q2 $1.51 vs $1.39) and its guides are 'at least' floors. The Q1 beat was paid (+14.2%); the Q2 beat was not (-9.7%).
findings.why_not_priced: The street bar has drifted down 4.28% in 60 days (Investing.com) but is still above the mechanical guide split. A Q3 that lands 'on guide' at ~$0.70 would read as a small miss on the headline. Sized small: Molina's 'at least' guides have been beaten twice this year, and the Medicaid peer read argues for upside.
findings.independence: Bar sources: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/analyst-projections-key-metrics-reveal-121506448.html and https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/molina-healthcare-earnings-in-focus-as-medicaid-pressures-mount-93CH-4894077. The guide arithmetic rests on the two SEC 8-K releases (Q1 and Q2).

findings.finding: The reaction function and positioning lean against the print. 7 of the last 8 MOH prints fell (median |move| 12.1%), including the Q2 2026 beat-and-raise (-9.67%). The stock goes in +13.6% over 20 days, at ~$215-220 against a $209 mean target on a consensus Hold, and at ~41x 2026 EPS per Investing.com.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: From the baseline: -9.67, +14.18, -25.51, -17.49, -16.84, -2.91, -5.48, -10.09. The only up move followed a quarter that was not preceded by a run-up of this size.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the skew is neutral (+0.12) and the put/call OI is low (0.33), so the options market is not braced for a fall after the run. Short interest is moderate (5.5% of shares outstanding, 4.8 days to cover), so a squeeze cannot do the work on the upside either.
findings.independence: The baseline history (SEC 8-K item 2.02 times) and the equibles short-interest page are separate from the article.

findings.finding: Molina's Q2 call set 2027 EPS building blocks at 'more than $10 per share before any Medicaid MCR improvement', with each 100 bp of Medicaid MCR worth ~$5/share and 2027 premium cut to ~$46.5B from the Investor Day $48B. Elevance said today that states are beginning 2027 rate work and 'expect to include more of the cost trend'. It also said it is planning for 'incremental acuity pressure' from rate and membership changes as work requirements arrive in January 2027, and that 'rates have certainly not fully caught up'. The Q3 call is where the 2027 framing will be updated.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance and next-year framing drove the four largest reactions in the baseline (-25.5% Feb 2026 on the 2026 guide, -17.5% Oct 2025, -16.8% Jul 2025, -9.7% Jul 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: The only 2027 consensus I could source is a stale $8.31 from a pre-Q1 Barchart preview (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1000411/here-s-what-to-expect-from-molina-healthcares-next-earnings-report), below the company's '>$10' floor. That suggests the published 2027 bar may lag the company framing, but I cannot confirm a current figure. At $215 the stock is ~21x the $10 floor, so the market is already paying for some Medicaid improvement. Two-sided: the expected value is small and the range is the widest in the file.
findings.independence: Elevance call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/21/elevance-elv-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/) for the 2027 state-rate and acuity read, a different document from Molina's call.

findings.finding: Molina announced on 2026-06-10 an intent to award of the HealthChoice Illinois Medicaid contract (one of six plans for ~3.1M beneficiaries), go-live 2027-01-01. Some aggregator text says it commences 2026-10-01, but the company release says January 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Contract wins have not moved prints. This one was known at the Q2 print, which fell 9.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced and inside the $46.5B 2027 premium outlook. It could matter only if the call sizes the contract or confirms no protest.

findings.finding: Peer Medicaid membership kept falling in Q3: Elevance 8.22M (-1.7% QoQ, -4.9% YoY), UNH Community & State -85K in the quarter. Molina's consensus already embeds -12.7% YoY total membership and premium revenue down ~5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Molina 'rarely misses revenue estimates' (Yahoo preview). Membership has not been the line that moved the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the consensus revenue estimates already show the decline. What is left is a 2027 membership guide hit from work requirements.

findings.finding: The first managed-care print in the Medicaid-heavy group this season sold its beat: Elevance's Q3 adjusted EPS of $6.99 against $4.70, with a raised guide, fell ~2% because only ~$0.50 was operating outperformance and $1.85 was non-operating. MOH followed it lower intraday ($219.72 to ~$215.1).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MOH's own Q2 2026 beat-and-raise was sold -9.7%. Today the tape punished the quality of the beat, not its size.
findings.why_not_priced: It shows the bar Molina's beat has to clear: an investment-income or prior-period-development beat may be discounted the same way. Partly visible in MOH's intraday slide today.
findings.independence: The MOH intraday price comes from Investing.com's 10:32 ET article ($219.72) against the baseline seal ($215.115, 17:10 UTC).

findings.finding: CMS published 2027 Medicare Advantage Star Ratings on 2026-10-08. Molina's last enrollment-weighted average was ~3.22 stars, and an analyst quoted by Investing.com called any Stars improvement 'not material to the stock' because Molina exits MAPD on 2027-01-01 (~224K lives).

baseline_tension: The peer evidence (ELV Medicaid and ACA, UNH MCR) leans positive and agrees with the +13.6% 20-day run-up, so much of it is likely priced. The skew is neutral and gives no direction. The name's 1-in-8 up history and the street bar above the company's implied quarter cut against a long, which leaves the sum near zero.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold its Q2 beat-and-raise): ELV Medicaid read-through 1.5 to 1.3, ELV ACA read-through 1.0 to 0.8, UNH 0.5 to 0.4. Partly offset by the 'what has worked' note that a peer printing after the company last spoke leaves consensus stale, so not cut further.

Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the bar rests on the company-implied ~$0.70 plus three estimate sources that disagree by ~10%. The bar-gap finding was eased from -1.0 to -0.8 because Molina's 'at least' guides were beaten twice this year.
Lesson 7: short interest checked (5.5% of shares, 4.8 days to cover). Not crowded, so the negative positioning finding stays at -1.5. Skew neutral.
Lesson 6 (exit window): Centene's 10-27 print and the 2027-01-01 Illinois and work-requirement effects moved to outside_window.
